title: The Hunter
text:
Before his name belonged to the stars, Orion belonged to the wild places.

He crossed the hills without fear. He could wait quietly, notice a track,
and follow it through the trees. Each successful hunt made his confidence grow.

In one old telling, that confidence became a boast. Orion believed no living
creature could stand against him. He spoke as though the whole Earth were his
to conquer.

But the Earth held lives he had never noticed. Beneath leaves and stones,
beyond the reach of his gaze, something small was waiting.
marginNotes: Keep this small pattern in mind. We will find it again.
glaux: Watch closely. Great strength can overlook small things.

title: The Scorpion
text:
The Earth heard Orion's boast.

She held the roots of trees and the creatures beneath them. She held the
paths he followed, and the lives that kept those paths alive.

She sent a scorpion.

Orion found it at his feet, small beside the hunter. Its tail curved over its
back. He faced it with the confidence that had carried him through every hunt.

The scorpion struck. Its sting ended Orion's life.

For once, his strength could take him no farther. The hunter's part in the
story on Earth was over. His place in the sky was still to come.
marginNotes: Ancient writers gave Orion different endings. This telling follows the scorpion story.
glaux: The smallest thing can change the whole story.

title: Among the Stars
text:
The tale did not end with the hunter's fall.

Zeus, ruler of the gods, placed the scorpion among the stars. Artemis, the
goddess of the hunt, asked him to remember Orion too.

So the hunter was given a place in the sky.

This is how one old telling explains the figure people imagined there.
Look at the raised arm, the broad shoulders, the belt across his middle.
The hunter can be pictured again, traced through the lights.

His story has travelled far beyond the hills. Now it has reached the page
you are holding open.
marginNotes: The hunter is an illustration. The star chart shows a pattern seen from Earth.
glaux: People gave the lights a story. Now look for the pattern.

title: Look Up
text:
The tale ends here. The stars are real.

Look near the middle of the chart. Three bright points sit close together,
in an almost-straight line. People picture them as the hunter's belt.

Begin there. Then let your eyes follow the pattern towards his shoulders
and feet. Near one shoulder, a reddish point has its own name: Betelgeuse.

The lines and the hunter belong to our picture of the sky. The stars are
faraway suns, seen from Earth.

You have followed the tale into a pattern you can recognise. Keep the belt
in mind. It will help you find Orion again.
glaux: Begin with the belt. Let the rest of Orion follow.
